relation: three separate representations: X14 x14_path_edges is seq_edge_list p (ordered list, conversion); X172 x172_path_edges and U7 path_edges are seq_edge_set s (finite support, conversion) and XE2 xe2_path_edge_set equals seq_edge_set p for every p (seq_edge_set_image); X178 x178_path_edge_set is seq_index_edge_set p (actual edges between first occurrences, conversion), equal to the support on duplicate-free walks
summary: Batch B, family B8 (`path_edges` / `path_edge_set`): all five helpers of the two normalized names, in three representation classes kept apart in registry and certificates. RAW ORDERED LIST: X14's `x14_path_edges p` (`map (fun e => [set e.1; e.2]) (zip p (behead p))`) now unfolds to `GTBase.walks_paths.seq_edge_list p`, convertible: order and multiplicity are kept, a repeated vertex gives a one-vertex set and a non-adjacent pair is listed. FINITE SUPPORT: X172's `x172_path_edges` and U7's `path_edges` (byte-identical bodies) now unfold to `seq_edge_set s` (`[set e in seq_edge_list s]`), convertible; XE2's `xe2_path_edge_set`, the existential image of the same pairs, now unfolds to `seq_edge_set p` too, equal for every sequence but not convertible (`seq_edge_set_image`; `xe2_path_edge_set_compat` is a proved equality and the #915 chain rewrites with it). FIRST-INDEX ACTUAL EDGES: X178's `x178_path_edge_set` (edges `x -- y` with both ends in `p` and adjacent FIRST indices, `U9.consec`) now unfolds to `seq_index_edge_set p`, convertible (`seq_index_consecutive` has `U9.consec`'s body; `U9.consec` itself is unchanged). It is a separate contract: it equals `seq_edge_set p :&: E(G)` on duplicate-free `p` and `seq_edge_set p` on duplicate-free walks (`seq_index_edge_set_uniq`, `seq_index_edge_set_walk`, `seq_index_edge_set_simple_path`), but not in general and not under reversal: in `K_3` the sequence `[:: 0; 1; 0; 2]` has the raw edge `{0, 2}` that its first-index set misses, while the reversed `[:: 2; 0; 1; 0]` has it (grounded in walks_paths.v and the public client). No uniqueness, adjacency, nonemptiness or loop guard is added to any raw contract.

Seven rows, eight intermediate declarations, all frozen with this family's helpers only: X14 `x14_rainbow_path` and Andersen's row; X62's cross-file `x62_edges_covered_by_paths` and its cover row; X172's bridge replacement, its complete `Inductive` closure (both constructors, renamed `generated_refl` / `generated_step`) and the finitely-generated row; U7's `immersion` (renamed `u7_immersion`: U7 names carry no wave prefix) and the colouring row; X174's negated immersion and its row with both halves (universal upper bound and existential attainment), the documented natural-subtraction caveat `(n - t) + 3` verbatim; XE2's edge-disjointness and #915; X178's decomposition predicate and the Gallai row. The four U7 grounding theorems keep their statements and proofs.

History. The complete X14 / X62 rows before every migration are family C6's `X14Original` / `X62Original` (GTMisc.migration.edge_colourings, C6 history 7b04105): they already freeze the raw path-edge list and the cover predicate with C6's properness over pre-M1 edges and B6's genuine path; their certificates hold unchanged by conversion and are reused here (C6's two complete rows as `original-statement` objects with C6's certificates, its frozen list, rainbow path and cover predicate as `historical` objects), not copied. New complete originals: `X172Original` (B2's frozen `x172_path_internal` with this family's frozen edge set, chain, closure and row), `XE2Original.erdos_915_statement` (B2's frozen internal disjointness with this family's frozen edge disjointness) and `X178Original` (B6's frozen `x178_path_seq` with this family's frozen edge set). Earlier partial snapshots (B2 X172 / #915, B6 X14 / X62 / X178, C6 X14 / X62) are unchanged; their reliance on this family's live helpers is listed below, and this family's per-row copies are listed in their reports. U7 and X174 had no earlier snapshot.

Kernel evidence, independent of this textual report: `Print All Dependencies` of every frozen statement and original contains no live helper or chain declaration of this family and none of `seq_edge_list`, `seq_edge_set`, `seq_index_edge_set`, while each live statement reaches its canonical and its alias (/srv/graph-theory-rocq/coordination/evidence/B8-path_edges/print_all_dependencies_summary.txt).

Baseline 048c768 is a private, not-for-integration merge of the B7 series fa3f5f4 with the C6 history 7b04105 (union of _CoqProject lines and of one simple_path summary sentence; no .v file differs from both parents). No statement text, doc block, manifest row or leg state changes (checked below).

Later migration: the cyclic extractors listed here as separate contracts (Cycle X9 `x9_cycle_edges`, Cycle X24 `x24_cycle_edge_seq`, Packing X25 `x25_cycle_edge_seq`, GTMisc X216 `x216_cycle_edges` and Cycle XE1 `xe1_cycle_edges`) were migrated by B11 (family cycle-edges) onto `GTBase.walks_paths.seq_cycle_edge_list`, `seq_cycle_edge_set` and `seq_cycle_graph_edge_set`, which keep the closing pair that this family's open `seq_edge_list` lacks; they are no longer untouched distinct variants.
